full.description: This image is a micrograph of gastrointestinal or colonic tissue stained with hematoxylin and eosin. It shows significant glandular crowding, architectural distortion, and cellular atypia lining the mucosal crypts. The epithelial cells exhibit nuclear enlargement, hyperchromasia, and loss of polarity, indicative of neoplastic transformation. These histological features are characteristic of colorectal adenocarcinoma or high-grade dysplasia.

blind.description: This image is a photomicrograph of lung tissue showing characteristic peribronchial noncaseating granulomas with many giant cells. The architectural changes and presence of multinucleated giant cells are prominent features within the interstitial spaces. These findings are strongly indicative of sarcoidosis as the most likely diagnosis.

random.description: This is a high-power microscopic image of tissue stained with hematoxylin and eosin. It shows atypical, crowded glandular structures lined by malignant epithelial cells with enlarged, hyperchromatic nuclei and prominent nucleoli. Mitotic figures and cellular debris are visible within the glandular lumen, suggestive of an adenocarcinoma. The morphological features are characteristic of a primary gastrointestinal adenocarcinoma or similar malignant epithelial neoplasm.
